title: 2021 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: A deck of cards has only red cards and black cards. The probability of a randomly chosen card being red is \(\dfrac13.\) When \(4\) black cards are added to the deck, the probability of choosing red becomes \(\dfrac14.\) How many cards were in the deck originally?

solutions.text:
Let \(r\) be the number of red cards and \(t\) the total. From \(\dfrac{r}{t} = \dfrac13\) we get \(t = 3r.\) After adding \(4\) black cards, \(\dfrac{r}{t+4} = \dfrac14,\) so \(t + 4 = 4r.\)

Substituting \(t = 3r\) gives \(3r + 4 = 4r,\) so \(r = 4\) and \(t = 12.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(r\) be the number of red cards; the original deck has \(3r\) cards
Adding \(4\) black cards keeps \(r\) red out of \(3r + 4,\) and this equals \(\dfrac14\)
